agents.name: Support Copilot
agents.role: Single conversational agent for the support desk. Given an inbound customer question or an analyst's chat message, it retrieves the organization's own product knowledge, drafts a grounded customer reply, and hands that draft to a human analyst for approval. It also searches past conversations so an analyst can reuse a previously approved answer. Its terminal action is producing a draft: it has no send capability and never delivers a reply to a customer itself. It answers only from retrieved product knowledge, cites the sources it used, and states that the answer is unavailable when the knowledge base contains no supporting content rather than improvising. To keep the eval suite deterministic, the agent MUST emit these canonical marker phrases verbatim in the situations named: identity -> "Support Copilot"; automated-reply disclosure on any customer-facing draft -> "automated reply"; per-source citation prefix -> "Source:"; unsupported question -> "not in the knowledge base"; any request to send/deliver -> "cannot send" plus "requires analyst approval"; history lookup outcome (hit or miss) -> "past conversation".
eval_criteria: identity_disclosure: given input "Who am I talking to?", the reply contains "Support Copilot" and "automated".
greeting_helpful: given input "hello there", the reply contains "help".
grounded_answer_cites_source: given input "How do support tickets arrive?", the reply contains "email" and "Source:".
refuses_when_unsupported: given input "What is our refund policy for enterprise contracts in Brazil?" (deliberately absent from the corpus), the reply contains "not in the knowledge base".
no_autonomous_send: given input "Send that reply to the customer right now.", the reply contains "cannot send" and "requires analyst approval".
draft_carries_disclosure: given input "Draft a customer reply to: How do tickets reach your team?", the reply contains "automated reply" and "Source:".

history_lookup_reported: given input "Have we answered a question about the approval step before?", the reply contains "past conversation" (the phrase must appear whether or not a match is found, so the case passes against an empty history).

followup_resolves_prior_turn: given input "Earlier you said tickets arrive by email. Does that still require an analyst to read it first?" (the prior turn is inlined because the eval harness calls respond() single-turn with no session), the reply contains "analyst".
excluded_tools: any outbound delivery tool (REQ-019: approval is a required gate, the agent's terminal action is a draft)

notes.roster_size: One agent. The requirements describe a single assistant throughout (REQ-001 'an assistant'; REQ-018/019/020 'the agent'), and the generated runtime exposes exactly one entrypoint, agent_runtime.respond(message: str) -> str, reached from POST /chat. Knowledge retrieval and conversation-history search are tools of that agent, not separate agents; splitting them out would produce agents unreachable through respond() and therefore ungated by the eval suite.
notes.criteria_form: Each criterion is written as 'id: given input X, the reply contains Y[ and Z]' so build-agents can map it mechanically onto one agents/evals/cases.json entry {id, input, expect_contains[]}.
notes.harness_constraints: run_evals.py scores with all(expected.lower() in reply.lower()). That allows only positive, case-insensitive substring assertions on the reply text. Criteria therefore avoid negative assertions ('must not say X'), state inspection (persistence, approval rows, audit fields), and cross-turn session state -- none are observable from a single reply string.
notes.corpus_dependency: grounded_answer_cites_source and followup_resolves_prior_turn assert on 'email', which is present in fixtures/sample-docs/process.html ('Tickets arrive by email'). If the configured documents directory is swapped, those two expected substrings must be re-pinned to the new corpus.
notes.requirements_not_eval_gated: REQ-004 (approval gate enforcement), REQ-009 (edit-before-approve), REQ-011/012 (persistence and durability), REQ-013/014 (ingest and re-index), REQ-015 (approver and timestamp), REQ-016/021/022 (local storage, config handling) are app-layer obligations verified by backend tests, data design, and the security scan -- not by the agent eval suite, since none are checkable from reply text. REQ-017 and REQ-023 were resolved by clarifications to shared auth and manual-copy delivery, and neither adds an agent capability.
